main_text.p: partim à metu, partim fpe & confidentia fumuntur.Sæpe enim ignaui qui funt,aut timidi, ad capeffenda negotia pœnæ inie-icto metu excitantur. Non etiam raró qui erectis funt præditi ingeniis fpe propofi-ta gratiæ,amoris,promotionis, excitátur, vt quæ in mandatis habent,& alacriter,& Collocatio argumentorum & sententiarum in singulis mandatoriarum epistolarum partibus.celeriter,expediant.Ad tractationem verò atque collocationem quod attinet, quatuor illa partibus conftat: Primum Exordium, quod fumitur,vel à fcribendi occafione negotij quod expediri volumus expo-fitione.lib.14.epift.5.6.Vel excufatione literarum breuitatis. lib.14. epift. 10.aut ratitatis. lib.14. epift. 6. vel expectatione & defiderio earundem.lib.16.epift.19.20. vel directo mandato.lib.16.epift.23. vel occupatione qua diffidentiæ fufpicioni occurritur.lib. 16.epift. 24. page.notes: The Greek phrase after "eft" is printed in a narrow, heavily worn type and is only partly legible; the reading shown is a best guess, marked [?]. The Greek word after "obliquè &" is also doubtful. The left margin notes "Propositiones." (beside "ritur.lib.") and "Confirmationes." (beside "23.Pars tertia") are printed in the margin but are not transcribed as notes here, because their placement is uncertain on the scan. The margin notes "Collocatio ... partibus." and "Exordia." are included where they stand. Page is slightly skewed and the left edge is shadowed.
